newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds trickle down, mood wary ahead of Buba.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds trickle down, mood wary ahead of Buba.

text.p: Danish bond prices trickled down on Monday echoing Friday's U.S. falls in a cautious market waiting for Tuesday's repo rate announcement by the Bundesbank with the wary mood expected to last the day out.
"The market has adopted a wait-and-see mood until Buba's repo announcement, with the strong dollar sparking speculation that a variable rate may be reintroduced," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.26 point from the opening at 113.24, yielding 5.97 percent, with the seven percent 2007 benchmark, due to take over on September 1, 0.31 lower at 106.15 with a 6.16 percent yield.
Turnover in the 2006 and 2007 tone-setting bonds was 1.2 billion and 765 million crowns respectively.
The 2006's September future fell 0.92 point to 112.92 with 59 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 was unchanged at 92.75.
The crown traded at 3.8100 per mark at 1150 GMT, unchanged from the opening.
The 2007's 10-year yield gap with Germany widened four points from the start to 54 bps.
